transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, this is the Valencia Health onboarding kickoff from Redwood, quick roll call?
[00:12] Sofia: hi this is Sofia Ramirez from product, Aaron here as CT-oh, Aaron: hey, Aaron Blake CTO, Lina: Lina Gomez platform eng, Marcus: Marcus Lee security, Ethan: Ethan Shaw from Redwood CSM, Priya: Priya Desai solutions eng, thanks all,
[01:05] Maya: cool agenda, we'll run through goals success criteria, access and security, staging plan and next steps, feel free to interrupt,
[02:20] Sofia: high level we're aiming to ship clinical summarization and triage assistant into our nurse intake flow by Q3, want low latency mostly, and sensitive PHI never leaves our VPC ideally,
[03:01] Priya: ok noted, we usually recommend private deployment for PHI heavy workloads but we also have Private (VPC) option and Dedicated if you want reserved capacity, there's tradeoffs on cost and maintenance,
[03:35] Aaron: can you clarify differences between dedicated and private? i'm hearing dedicated is reserved gpu pools in redwood infra and private is control-plane in our vpc?
[03:50] Priya: yeah so dedicated gives you reserved capacity on our infra with tenancy and predictable throughput, private puts the control plane inside your VPC or on-prem, you manage networking and keys, redwood still manages runtime optionally,
[04:28] Marcus: security-wise we need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, audit logs and SSO, also rotation of API keys, can you hook into our key management,
[04:45] Maya: yes we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private, we can do customer-managed keys for encryption at rest and envelope keys for tokenization, we'll send the docs,
[05:10] Ethan: also audit logs and per-route tracing are available in the console, retention is configurable, Marcus: okay what about data residency?
[05:30] Priya: we have region pinning and you can restrict routing so requests never leave eu/na etc, we'll capture the req in notes and set up policies,
[06:02] Lina: from platform side we need IP allowlist for peering, do you support VPC peering or private link? specifics re: Azure vs AWS,
[06:20] Priya: we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink today, Azure Private Link roadmap is there, we'll capture your cloud provider and do a network plan,
[07:00] Sofia: timeline wise we're targetting POC within 6 weeks and production later in Q3, so initial pilot must cover 10k sessions a day,
[07:18] Priya: for throughput we can size Dedicated pools, and we can provide model/quantization recommendations to hit latency SLOs, do you have target latency per request?
[07:40] Sofia: sub 500ms on median is target, 95th under 1.2s, but we can trade cost vs latency,
[08:02] Priya: great we'll run an initial benchmark in staging with a representative prompt set, that will guide batch sizes and kernel selection,
[08:30] Aaron: on models, do you host open models only or have variants? we want to pin a model version for consistency,
[08:42] Maya: you can pin model versions, we carry curated open models and verified performance profiles, and can fallback to compatible variants under outage,
[09:05] Marcus: on compliance, we need SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning, RBAC and auditability for admin actions,
[09:22] Ethan: SSO + SCIM supported, we'll need the IdP metadata and a list of admin users, SCIM can automate provisioning, RBAC is granular per-route and per-team,
[09:50] Priya: small note transcription, excuse me, we often see slight naming mismatches in transcriptions, not relevant but just FYI,
[10:12] Lina: what's the onboarding flow? do you do data ingestion or just API integration?
[10:25] Maya: onboarding typically: 1) security and network setup (SSO, VPC), 2) staging access and API keys, 3) pilot bench & quality evals, 4) roll to prod with runbook and training,
[10:45] Sofia: training for clinicians is key, want a 90-minute session on prompt tuning and safety guardrails,
[10:55] Ethan: yes we'll do a tailored training session, plus a short admin walkthrough for your ops team,
[11:20] Marcus: quick question on logs and PHI, can you mask PII in logs or redact PHI?
[11:32] Priya: we support configurable redaction and prefix KV caching that can be disabled for PHI flows, also offer end-to-end encryption,
[12:05] Aaron: how do you handle key rotation without downtime?
[12:15] Maya: we support zero-downtime key rotation via envelope keys and dual-key support during rotation window, we'll document the steps,
[12:45] Sofia: for pilot success criteria we'll measure: accuracy of summaries (human eval), latency SLOs, integration stability and security sign-off,
[13:05] Priya: noted, we'll help create an eval harness and quality monitors, Redwood Optimize will give quantization and model recommendations to hit cost targets,
[13:40] Lina: on the sandbox, how do we get API keys and limits? we need token-based access, and dev env shouldn't hit prod limits,
[13:58] Ethan: we'll provision a staging org for Valencia, with scoped API keys and rate limits, also provide cost estimates,
[14:30] Maya: sharing the onboarding checklist now in chat (link), plus security packet and network worksheet,
[15:02] Sofia: perfect, also want to involve legal for DPA and acceptable use, do you have templates?
[15:18] Maya: yes we'll attach DPA and subprocessors list, procurement may need SLA and support tiers which we can include,
[16:00] Priya: tech deep dive will include benchmark plan: sample prompts, dataset size, target seq lengths, we'll run local and cloud tests,
[16:32] Aaron: can we run an on-prem testbed? some of our data can't leave the building,
[16:45] Priya: yes on-prem deployments are possible but timeline and ops overhead differ, we'll scope it in the technical deep dive,
[17:10] Marcus: for SOC2 evidence, what's the typical lead time?
[17:25] Ethan: we can provide our SOC2 Type II report and ISO attestation immediately, timelines for audits vary but docs are standard,
[17:52] Sofia: ok next steps, can we get a consolidated runbook and roles matrix?
[18:05] Maya: yes action items we'll list after call, Ethan will own cadence, Priya will own staging runbook and benchmarks,
[18:25] Lina: can you include network CIDR ranges and sample peering templates,
[18:38] Priya: absolutely, will include AWS VPC peering example and PrivateLink config,
[19:00] Aaron: any blockers we should highlight? Marcus: we need internal approval for data residency and DPA, that might be a gating item,
[19:22] Maya: understood, we'll treat procurement docs as high priority,
[20:00] Sofia: schedule wise let's get the tech deep dive next week, week of 4/28, and pilot kickoff first week of May,
[20:20] Ethan: i'll send invites and template for prompts and evals,
[21:15] Maya: great, final recap: send onboarding checklist + security packet, schedule deep dive with Priya, set up staging org and API keys, weekly check-ins starting May 5,
[21:40] Marcus: thanks all, appreciate the clarity everyone,
[22:00] Sofia: thanks,
[22:10] Meeting closed.
